title: [CLO Beginner's Guide] Materials_Attachments
description: CLO Beginner's Guide, material-related series courses. Understand CLO fabrics and master the methods of representing garment materials, including buttons, textures, interfacing, edgings, zippers, topstitching, sewing wrinkles, and hardware accessories. Take you deep into learning how to proficiently use CLO materials.
transcript:
Next, add a copy of the D-circle to the back of the model.  
Open the copy of Connect, select the hardware, and select Rings.  
Find the D-circle.  
Double-click to add it to the object window.  
Drag the D-circle from the object window to the 3D window.  
In the open copy window, you can choose the location of the D-circle,  
either the original location or the coordinate location 0, 0.  
Here, select the original location and the location where the D-circle is stored.  
Use the move tool to select the D-circle.  
There are three tools in the upper right corner.  
Next, we will apply these three tools.  
First, single-click to start the first quick arrangement tool.  
When the mouse moves over the costume,  
you can see the gray shadow of the D-circle moving with the mouse,  
indicating the position where the D-circle will be placed.  
When you approach the target location,  
you can easily and quickly place the D-circle near the target location.  
Again, single-click to start the third glue tool.  
At the appropriate position,  
single-click to move the D-circle to this position.  
You can use the positioning ball to slightly adjust the D-circle.  
In the object window, select the D-circle component,  
and in the property editor,  
select its specification property.  
First, you can enter the name of the component,  
product number, and other information.  
The proportion in the specification can be adjusted  
to the size of the component along the X, Y, and Z axes.  
The default fixed proportion is used.  
You can adjust the size according to this proportion.  
In the weight column, set the weight of the component.  
The input weight value will be reflected in the simulation.  
Under the material section, you can set the material type of the component.  
In addition, there is another way to adjust the size of the component.  
After selecting the component with the move tool,  
single-click on this square icon.  
The coordinates change to the shrink adjustment coordinates.  
Place the mouse on the red, green, or blue coordinate axis separately.  
When the left mouse button is pressed and the mouse is moved,  
the size of the component in the corresponding direction can be changed.  
If you want to increase or decrease the proportion uniformly,  
place the mouse on the gray, three-dimensional square in the middle.  
The mouse pointer changes to a diagonal arrowhead.  
Press and hold the left mouse button and move the mouse,  
and the proportion can be adjusted according to the size of the component.  
After adjusting the size,  
single-click on the icon to close these coordinates.  
The terrain ring is in the selected state.  
The property editor can edit its conflict thickness and rigidity.  
The component simulation is carried out below.  
The component simulation can perform the movement of the B pin,  
and interact stably with the 3D clothing.  
Before simulation,  
right-click on the component first,  
to ensure that activation is enabled.  
Then,  
click to simulate.  
You can see the terrain ring colliding and simulating naturally between the panels.  
After stabilization,  
close the simulation.  
The terrain ring is added and completed.  
Right-click on the terrain ring again.  
The simulation option is removed from activation.  
There are two other options:  
Freeze and Reactivate.  
For the component,  
if you only want it to collide with the panel,  
but not move,  
select Freeze.  
If you want to stop both collision and simulation at the same time,  
select Reactivate.  
Finally, the completed component will be saved.  
Select it in the object window.  
In the property editor,  
click Save.  
Save the component in the .trm file format,  
so that it can be used later.  
Now,  
model a state of the area.  
Select this state.  
Go back to the model.  
Select the .trm function.  
Select the .trm object from the .trm tutorial.  
Select.  
Select .trm.  
Click.

chunks.content: ## Adding and Positioning the D-Circle Component in CLO This section explains how to add a D-circle component to a CLO model, including selecting, placing, and positioning it accurately using the move and quick arrangement tools. It covers component placement techniques and interface navigation relevant to hardware attachments. - Open a copy of the model in Connect. - Select the hardware category, then choose "Rings." - Locate the D-circle and double-click it to add it to the object window. - Drag the D-circle from the object window into the 3D window. - In the copy window, select the original location option to place the D-circle at its stored coordinates rather than coordinate 0,0. - Use the Move Tool located in the upper right corner of the interface to manipulate the D-circle. - There are three positioning tools: 1. **Quick Arrangement Tool**: Single-click to start. Moving the mouse over the costume shows a gray shadow of the D-circle moving with the cursor, indicating where it will be placed. This facilitates quick, approximate placement near the target. 2. **Glue Tool**: Single-click to activate. Click again at the precise position to snap the D-circle exactly onto the model. 3. **Positioning Ball**: Allows fine adjustment of the D-circle’s placement after snapping it. ## Editing Component Properties and Specifications This section details how to modify the D-circle component’s properties including name, product number, size, weight, and material. It also explains two methods for resizing components in the 3D workspace. - Select the D-circle component in the object window. - In the property editor, open the specification tab. - Enter metadata such as component name and product number. - Adjust the component size proportions along the X, Y, and Z axes. The default setting maintains fixed proportions but can be overridden for custom sizing. - Set the component weight, which affects simulation behavior. - Choose the material type under the material section. ### Resizing Methods 1. **Property Editor Scaling**: Adjust X, Y, Z proportions numerically. 2. **Interactive Scale Tool**: - Select the component and activate the move tool. - Click the square icon to switch to shrink adjustment coordinates. - Drag the red, green, or blue axis handles to adjust size in one dimension. - Drag the gray three-dimensional square in the center to scale uniformly in all directions. - Click the icon again to exit resizing mode. ## Simulating Component Behavior and Collision This section describes how to run and control physical simulations of the D-circle component to ensure proper interaction and collision with garments. - Before starting simulation, right-click the component and ensure "Activation" is enabled. - Click the simulate button to start the physics simulation. - Observe natural collision and interaction of the terrain ring (D-circle) with garment panels. - After the simulation stabilizes, close the simulation window. - Right-click the terrain ring component again to toggle simulation options: - **Freeze**: Allows collision detection but prevents component movement. - **Reactivate**: Stops both collision and simulation.

chunks.content: ## Simulating Component Behavior and Collision This section describes how to run and control physical simulations of the D-circle component to ensure proper interaction and collision with garments. - Before starting simulation, right-click the component and ensure "Activation" is enabled. - Click the simulate button to start the physics simulation. - Observe natural collision and interaction of the terrain ring (D-circle) with garment panels. - After the simulation stabilizes, close the simulation window. - Right-click the terrain ring component again to toggle simulation options: - **Freeze**: Allows collision detection but prevents component movement. - **Reactivate**: Stops both collision and simulation. These options control the component’s dynamic behavior in the simulation environment. ## Saving and Reusing Component Files (.trm) This section covers saving the completed component and applying it to different model states using CLO’s .trm file format. - Select the finished component in the object window. - In the property editor, click the Save button. - Save the component as a .trm file for future use. - To apply the saved component: - Select the desired model state. - Return to the model workspace. - Use the .trm function to load the saved .trm file from the tutorial directory. - Select and apply the .trm component to the model. This workflow facilitates modular hardware attachment reuse across different garments or design iterations.
